title: Podkletnov's gravity shielding and a Schauberger/Soviet lineage

plain: A researcher named Eugene Podkletnov, working at the University of Tampere in Finland in the 1990s, claimed that objects lost weight above spinning superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance when very cold. Michels tells this himself, drawing on The Hunt for Zero Point, a book by the journalist Nick Cook, and he sets Podkletnov in a line of work going back through Soviet research to the Austrian inventor Viktor Schauberger. If the claim held, it would mean a way to cancel part of gravity, which is why it comes up in talk of antigravity propulsion.
